speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the nature of your wrist pain and when the fever and skin lesions first appeared? Are the lesions painful, itchy, or blistering?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you notice any expanding red rash with central clearing, known as a bull's-eye rash, on your skin during the camping trip or since returning? Have you noticed any tick bites or felt any muscle aches or headaches alongside the joint pain?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the camping history in Minnesota and the violaceous lesions, I am concerned about Spotted Fever Group Rickettsia or Ehrlichiosis. REQUEST TEST: Rickettsia serology, Ehrlichia serology, CBC, and CRP.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal Rickettsia and Ehrlichia serologies make those diagnoses unlikely, so I need to reconsider the etiology. Have you had any recent respiratory infections or sore throat, and have you noticed any heart palpitations or shortness of breath?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history. Social history: Admits to being sexually active with one female partner who uses a diaphragm for contraception. Recently went on a camping trip to Minnesota.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the sexually active history and acute monoarticular arthritis, I must rule out gonococcal infection despite the atypical rash. REQUEST TEST: Nucleic Acid Amplification Test for Neisseria gonorrhoeae, blood cultures, and synovial fluid analysis.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Nucleic Acid Amplification Test for Neisseria gonorrhoeae: Positive; Blood cultures: Pending at the time of examination; Synovial fluid analysis: WBC >50,000 /μL (markedly elevated), Gram Stain: Gram-negative diplococci seen

speaker: Doctor
text: The positive NAAT, gram-negative diplococci in the synovial fluid, and characteristic skin lesions confirm the diagnosis. DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Gonococcal Infection
